citation.authors: Wyndham CH, Williams CG, Morrison JF, Heyns AJ et al

record.population: Groups of 10 highly acclimatised Bantu men resting in hot, humid rooms
record.design: Laboratory exposure study at 96 to 104 degrees F wet bulb, with criteria for withdrawal
record.finding: Rectal temperature rose steadily at 102 and 104 F wet bulb and reached a plateau at lower temperatures. Sweat rate rose from 130 ml per hour at 96 F to 875 ml per hour at 104 F; water intake lagged behind sweating at the highest temperatures. There was no comparison group in the abstract.
record.note: No comparison with other ancestry groups, so it does not show a difference; 1968.
